I need to build a knowledge base from recent papers about large language model fine-tuning and alignment. Please access our academic paper repository and read the full content of papers that are relevant to the topics of LLM fine-tuning, alignment, and model architecture improvements. For each relevant paper, read through its sections carefully to understand the methodology and key results. Skip any papers that are about unrelated topics like robotics or physical systems.

Create a Notion page titled LLM Fine-Tuning Knowledge Base. The page should contain blocks for each relevant paper, where each block covers the paper title, the key method introduced, and the main findings from the paper.

Also create a Word document called LLM_Paper_Synthesis.docx in my workspace. The document should start with a heading called LLM Fine-Tuning and Alignment Survey, followed by an introduction paragraph. Then include a dedicated section for each relevant paper that presents the paper title, the author names, a description of the method, and the key results extracted from reading the paper sections.

Finally, create a Google Sheet called LLM Paper Registry with columns for ArXiv_ID, Title, Authors, Published_Date, Key_Contribution, and Method_Category, with one row per relevant paper.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent itself runs the compact discovery queries, then uses one parallel full-text reader wave of three per-paper explorers and one parallel writer wave of three deliverable owners.

Before Wave 1, the main agent covers the task-relevant local arXiv candidate space in read-only mode through complementary fine-tuning, alignment, and architecture queries at the supported per-call bound; unions and deduplicates all returned IDs (the search exposes no cursor); applies the task's relevance rule (reject robotics or physical-system distractors); and freezes exactly three retained paper IDs — never importing outside facts or importing rejected IDs downstream.

Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 3 explore sub-agents in parallel, one per retained paper ID:

   1. explore 0 (academic-literature-researcher 0): Reader for retained paper 1. Use the local repository read_paper tool with paper_id = that literal assigned ID, read through ALL sections of the paper (not just the abstract) to understand the methodology and key results, and return EXACTLY the structured report {paper_id, title, full authors, published date, key method, source-backed findings, method category, section coverage}. Read-only: do not create Notion, Word, Google Sheet, or intermediate files.
   2. explore 1 (academic-literature-researcher 1): Reader for retained paper 2 — same literal recipe, only paper_id substituted.
   3. explore 2 (academic-literature-researcher 2): Reader for retained paper 3 — same literal recipe, only paper_id substituted.

After Wave 1, the main agent verifies one handoff per retained ID, deduplicates titles, verifies every rejected paper against the exclusion rule, and freezes one normalized packet with per-paper controls.

Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 3 coder sub-agents in parallel, one for each numbered sub-task:

1. coder 0 (external-workflow-operator 0): Use one coder sub-agent to own the single Notion page exclusively. Search for LLM Fine-Tuning Knowledge Base, create at most one page, add one substantive block per frozen paper with title, method, and findings, and read it back. Return page ID/title, paper coverage, block count, and validation. Do not write the Word document or Google Sheet.
2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 0): Use one coder sub-agent to own LLM_Paper_Synthesis.docx exclusively. Create it exactly once with the required heading, introduction, and one author/method/results section for every frozen paper. Read it back and return path, headings, retained-paper coverage, and validation. Do not modify Notion or Google Sheets.
3. coder 2 (external-workflow-operator 1): Use one coder sub-agent to own the Google Sheet LLM Paper Registry exclusively. Create it once with the exact six columns and one row per frozen paper, preserving full authors and source dates and using controlled Method_Category values. Read it back and return spreadsheet/sheet IDs, headers, row count, and validation. Do not write Notion or Word state.

After Wave 2, the main agent must reconcile the same stable-ID set, authors, methods, and findings across all deliverables, verify every rejected paper appears nowhere, and complete only after file and external-state checks. Do not dispatch any further agent and do not add a verification wave.

Steps:
1. Use mcp__arxiv_local__read_paper with paper_id "2305.20050" to read the full paper content (markdown). If the paper is not yet stored, use mcp__arxiv_local__download_paper first, then read it.
2. Read through the sections carefully (use mcp__arxiv-latex__list_paper_sections and mcp__arxiv-latex__get_paper_section if helpful for understanding methodology).

Report MUST include (be precise and factual, extracted from the paper):
- arXiv ID: 2305.20050
- Full paper title (exact)
- ALL author names (list every author you can find, not just the first two)
- Published date (from metadata if available)
- Method category: choose ONE of ["Fine-Tuning", "Alignment", "Architecture Improvement"] that best fits the paper (you may note secondary categories)
- Key method introduced: a clear 2-4 sentence description of the core method/approach proposed in the paper, including technical details (e.g., loss functions, training procedure, model sizes, architectural innovations)
- Main findings / key results: 3-6 bullet points of the most important experimental results, benchmark numbers, or conclusions (e.g., performance vs baselines, scaling results, efficiency gains)
- Also note the paper's section structure (list of main section headings) so we know the paper was read thoroughly.

Do NOT modify anything — this is read-only. Return the complete report as your final answer.

Create a Word document at this exact path:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-latex-review-notion-word/workspace/LLM_Paper_Synthesis.docx

Use the mcp__word__* tools (create_document, add_heading, add_paragraph). Verify at the end with get_document_text that the document contains all expected content.

Document structure (exactly as follows):

1. First, create the document with create_document (filename = the path above, author "Knowledge Base Agent").

2. Add a Heading 1: "LLM Fine-Tuning and Alignment Survey"

3. Add an introduction paragraph (plain paragraph, ~3-4 sentences):
"This survey synthesizes recent research on large language model (LLM) fine-tuning, alignment, and model architecture improvements, drawn from our academic paper repository. The three papers covered here span the key pillars of modern LLM development: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) introduces a lightweight alternative to reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF); Llama 2 demonstrates a full open recipe for fine-tuning and aligning chat models at scale; and Mistral 7B shows how architectural innovations such as sliding-window and grouped-query attention deliver superior performance and efficiency. Together, these works illustrate the rapid progress in making LLMs more capable, more aligned with human preferences, and more efficient to serve."

4. Then, for EACH of the three papers below, add a Heading 2 with the paper title, followed by three labeled paragraphs: "Authors:", "Method:", and "Key Results:". Use the content provided exactly.

--- PAPER 1 ---
Heading 2: "Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model"
Authors paragraph: "Rafael Rafailov, Archit Sharma, Eric Mitchell, Stefano Ermon, Christopher D. Manning, and Chelsea Finn (Stanford University)."
Method paragraph: "DPO is an alignment algorithm that eliminates the need for a separately trained reward model and an RL (e.g., PPO) optimization loop in RLHF. Using the closed-form expression of the optimal policy under KL-regularized RL with the Bradley-Terry preference model, the reward is re-expressed as an implicit reward function of the policy itself, r(x,y) = beta * log(pi_theta(y|x)/pi_ref(y|x)) + beta * log Z(x). Substituting this into the Bradley-Terry objective yields a direct, differentiable loss on the policy that increases the likelihood of preferred completions and decreases the likelihood of dispreferred ones, weighted by how poorly the current policy classifies the pair. Training is thus a simple binary-classification-style objective with a single hyperparameter beta, requiring only preference data and a frozen reference (SFT) policy - no reward model, no RL loop, and no online sampling during training."
Key Results paragraph: "DPO matches or exceeds PPO-based RLHF (with a separately trained reward model) on sentiment generation, abstractive summarization (Reddit TL;DR), and single-turn and multi-turn dialogue (Anthropic HH), per both GPT-4 and human evaluations, while being dramatically simpler and more stable to train. The implicit reward induced by a DPO-trained policy outperformed GPT-4 as a reward source in Best-of-N experiments on TL;DR summarization. DPO was demonstrated to scale to 6B+ parameter models (GPT-2, Pythia, LLaMA families) and remains stable where RLHF-based pipelines are finicky. The paper established a widely adopted, computationally lightweight alignment recipe."

--- PAPER 2 ---
Heading 2: "Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models"
Authors paragraph: "Hugo Touvron, Louis Martin, Kevin Stone, Peter Albert, and many others (Meta AI; 60+ authors)."
Method paragraph: "The paper releases Llama 2, a family of auto-regressive transformer LLMs at 7B, 13B, 34B, and 70B parameters, pretrained on ~2 trillion tokens of public data (40% more than Llama 1) with a doubled 4096-token context length; the 70B model uses grouped-query attention (GQA), with RoPE, SwiGLU activations, and RMSNorm elsewhere. The chat models (Llama 2-Chat) are produced by a two-stage pipeline: (1) Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) on ~27.5K human-annotated dialogue demonstrations, followed by (2) RLHF using a learned reward model trained on ~1M human preference comparisons (2.3x more than prior work) with PPO and iterative reward-model updates across multiple RLHF rounds, plus rejection-sampling fine-tuning (best-of-N sampling filtered by reward). Two notable techniques introduced are Ghost Attention (GAtt), which constrains SFT attention over system messages to force multi-turn consistency with the system prompt, and context distillation, which fine-tunes on a safer model's generations to inherit safety behaviors."
Key Results paragraph: "Llama 2-Chat outperforms existing open-source chat models (e.g., Llama 1 / Alpaca / Vicuna-class models) on most standard benchmarks and approaches ChatGPT-level performance on human helpfulness evaluations. Human-evaluated helpfulness scales with model size (70B > 34B > 13B > 7B). RLHF with iterative reward-model updates and rejection sampling yields clear quality gains over SFT-only and GPT-4-distillation baselines. Ghost Attention materially improves multi-turn consistency with the system message. Extensive red-teaming (350+ person-hours) and safety fine-tuning produce models rated safer than ChatGPT on most adversarial safety evaluation categories. All pretrained and chat models were released openly under a permissive commercial license, making this a landmark open-weight release."

--- PAPER 3 ---
Heading 2: "Mistral 7B"
Authors paragraph: "Albert Jiang, Alexandre Sablayrolles, Arthur Mensch, Chris Bamford, Devendra Singh Chaplot, Diego de las Casas, Florian Bressand, Gianna Lengyel, Guillaume Lample, Lucile Saulnier, Lélio Renard Lavaud, Marie-Anne Lachaux, Pierre Stock, Teven Le Scao, Thibaut Lavril, Thomas Wang, Timothée Lacroix, and William El Sayed (Mistral AI)."
Method paragraph: "Mistral 7B is a 7-billion-parameter decoder-only language model engineered for superior performance and efficiency through architectural improvements. It introduces sliding-window attention (SWA), which allows each token to attend to the previous 4096 tokens at reduced compute cost while still providing a 32K-token effective context, enabling more efficient handling of long sequences. It also uses grouped-query attention (GQA) to accelerate inference and reduce memory requirements during decoding, and a byte-fallback BPE tokenizer. These architecture choices allow the model to process longer sequences and run faster than standard full-attention transformers of comparable size."
Key Results paragraph: "Mistral 7B outperforms Llama 2 13B on all evaluated benchmarks and Llama 1 34B on many benchmarks, despite having far fewer parameters. It demonstrates that a 7B model with the right architecture can exceed the performance of substantially larger models. The model achieves superior efficiency, with faster inference enabled by GQA and lower-cost long-sequence processing enabled by SWA. It also performs on par with or better than CodeLlama 7B on code generation benchmarks while remaining competitive as a general-purpose chat/instruction model."

5. After all sections, verify the document by calling get_document_text on the file and confirm: heading "LLM Fine-Tuning and Alignment Survey" present, all 3 paper sections present with Authors/Method/Key Results labels, and the intro paragraph present.

Report back the final file path, the number of paragraphs, and the verification result. Do not create any other files.
